result.topic_en: Methodological remarks on formulas and calculation as means versus ends, followed by notes on prime number literature, the limit behaviour of a sum related to the series $\sum \ln x^n$, and a plan to rework Dirichlet's proof of infinitely many primes in arithmetic progressions.

items.english: By means of the series $\sum \ln x^n$ one can compute $\lim \sum_{\varepsilon=0} \frac{1}{p(1+\varepsilon p)}$, i.e. state how this limit becomes infinite.

items.english: Work through thoroughly Dirichlet's proof of the infinitude of primes in arithmetic progression.

items.quote:
1) Ob nicht
der Beweis, dass $L_{+1}$ und $L_{-1}$ $\neq 0$ sind unnötig ist, wenn man
an Stelle dessen direkt durch den Satz der Kreisteilungs-
gl. (dass die linke [-x-] Seite derselben nur Primzahlen von der
Form $kp+1$ darstellt) [-x-] [-dass man-] $\sum^{p<N} \frac{1}{p q}$ [-#-] [-p-]$(q = kp+1)$ berechnet,
[-wie-], wie es Tschebyscheff und Mertens für $\sum^{p<N} \frac{1}{q}$ ($q$ = jeder Primzahl)
items.english: 1) Whether the proof that $L_{+1}$ and $L_{-1}$ are $\neq 0$ is not unnecessary if instead one computes directly, by means of the theorem on the cyclotomic equation (that its left-hand side represents only primes of the form $kp+1$), $\sum^{p<N} \frac{1}{pq}$ $(q = kp+1)$, as Chebyshev and Mertens did for $\sum^{p<N} \frac{1}{q}$ ($q$ = every prime).
